summary.text: A 38-year-old man without reported underlying disease was referred to a gastroenterologist on July 29, 2023 with weakness, lethargy, anorexia and vague epigastric pain. A complete blood count showed pancytopenia and he was referred to a hematologist.

Bone marrow aspiration was done for suspected acute leukemia; flow cytometry ruled out acute lymphoid and acute myeloid leukemia, and microscopy showed erythroid hyperplasia, megaloid changes and dysplastic neutrophils. He was hospitalized 48 hours later for progressive weakness and lethargy.

Hospital work-up found TSH 200 mIU/L and serum B12 110 pg/dl, with negative direct and indirect Coombs tests, no significant lymphoma on CT, urine copper 110 ug/dl and folate 4.2 ng/dl. Primary hypothyroidism and vitamin B12 deficiency were confirmed.

On hospital day 2 hemoglobin fell to 5.9 gr/dL and one packed cell was prepared, after which hemoglobin was 6.8 gr/dL; he developed fever, thrombophlebitis and a positive blood culture with septicemia. Transesophageal echo showed no vegetation and intravenous meropenem was prescribed for 14 days.

Vitamin B12 was started on day 3 with endoscopy and stomach biopsy showing no evidence of pernicious anemia. On day 5 an episode on upward gaze resolved when he was laid down with legs raised; Holter monitoring, CD55/CD59 flow cytometry, haptoglobin and MR venography were used to rule out cardiac syncope, PNH, Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia and cerebral sinus thrombosis. Levothyroxine was started on day 6.

A peripheral smear one day before discharge showed hyper-segmented neutrophils without evidence of myeloid dysplasia syndrome, and counts had risen compared with the initial slides. After discharge he took levothyroxine and vitamin B12; at the August 21, 2023 clinic visit platelets, WBC, MCV and hemoglobin had recovered further.
Daily CBC values from 29 July to 21 August 2023 are recorded as dated observations: WBC, RBC, platelets, hemoglobin and MCV in all columns and LDH where reported.
